title: Chicken Adobo
summary: Chicken is browned, then gently braised in a tangy soy and vinegar sauce until tender, before the sauce is reduced to a dark, glossy glaze.
equipment: large heavy casserole or deep lidded frying pan (28 cm)

ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

ingredients.note: about 1 tbsp; optional, rounds off the vinegar

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Pat the chicken dry, then heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until deep golden and the fat has rendered out, then turn and cook for a further 2 minutes before lifting it out. Starting skin-side down gives the fat time to melt and the skin time to crisp, rather than steaming in its own moisture.

steps.title: Fry the aromatics
steps.text: Once most of the fat is poured off, leaving about a tablespoon in the pan, add the garlic, peppercorns and bay leaves over medium heat. Cook for 1 minute, just until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic catch and turn bitter.

steps.title: Boil the sauce base
steps.text: Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar, water and sugar, then bring to a boil and let it bubble for 2 minutes without stirring. This brief hard boil softens vinegar's raw, sharp edge before the chicken goes back in.

steps.title: Braise until tender
steps.text: Return the chicken to the pan skin-side up, cover, and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes until it's tender and the thigh meat reads at least 74°C, ideally closer to 80°C for dark meat. Keep the heat low enough for a lazy simmer, since a hard boil would toughen the meat before it has time to soften.

steps.title: Reduce the sauce
steps.text: With the chicken lifted out onto a tray, boil the sauce uncovered for 5-8 minutes until it has reduced by about half and turned glossy. This concentrates the flavour into a sauce that clings to the chicken rather than pooling thinly around it.

steps.title: Crisp the skin (optional)
steps.text: For crisper skin, grill (broiler) the chicken skin-side up for 3-4 minutes until it browns further, keeping a close eye so it doesn't burn under the direct heat.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Return the chicken to the reduced sauce to coat, then scatter over the sliced spring onions. Serve with steamed rice - adobo is one of those dishes that tastes even better the next day, once the flavours have had time to settle.

tips: Don't rush the browning step - well-rendered, golden skin gives the sauce a deeper flavour than chicken added to the pan raw.
Boil the vinegar and soy mixture briefly before the chicken goes back in; this takes the raw harshness off the vinegar.
Check the chicken reaches at least 74°C (ideally 80°C for thighs) rather than judging by time alone, since pan and chicken sizes vary.
If the sauce looks thin after braising, reduce it uncovered rather than thickening it with flour - that's what gives adobo its characteristic glossy finish.
Leftovers taste better the next day, so this is a good dish to make ahead.
storage: Store in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the hob or in the microwave until piping hot and the chicken reaches 74°C throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
